body:
## Context / Why
Squeal's slow tier ran a package test suite in a fresh worktree that had never been built. The suite needs a build output that did not exist, so 9 tests failed in 9 different shapes, from "Cannot find module …/dist/index.js" to an unrelated regex mismatch. The agent ruled out each one as environmental before it could trust the run. CI builds first, so it never sees this.

## What needs to be done
Let a tier declare a precondition, such as a file that must exist or a command that must succeed, and when it is not met report one clear "skipped: <reason>" result for the tier instead of running it. Whether Squeal should also run a declared build step first is open; decide it during design.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A tier in `squeal.config.json` can declare a precondition, documented in the README
- [ ] When the precondition fails, Squeal reports the tier once as skipped with the configured message and runs none of its tests
- [ ] When the precondition passes, the tier runs as it does today
- [ ] A test covers both cases
title: [Task]: Skip a tier with one message when its precondition is not met
